title: Metadata and security functions in Fabric Warehouse and SQL analytics endpoint
summary: Most name-to-ID metadata functions work in Fabric: OBJECT_ID, OBJECT_NAME, SCHEMA_NAME, DB_NAME, DB_ID, COL_NAME, COLUMNPROPERTY, OBJECTPROPERTY(EX), TYPE_NAME, SERVERPROPERTY, DATABASEPROPERTYEX and @@VERSION. Several SQL Server habits fail to compile. These include USER_ID, DATABASE_PRINCIPAL_ID, SUSER_ID, ORIGINAL_LOGIN, COL_LENGTH, APP_NAME, HOST_NAME and SESSIONPROPERTY. Identity functions return Entra names (UPNs), not DOMAIN\user. Property functions return sql_variant and need an explicit CAST. Workspace roles are not database roles, so role checks can quietly return 0.

claims.statement: USER_ID is not supported in Fabric and fails at compile time. To get the current database user, use USER_NAME() or CURRENT_USER. To get a principal id, look it up in sys.database_principals.
claims.sql_server: USER_ID() returns the int principal id of the current database user (deprecated, but it still works).
claims.alternative: SELECT principal_id FROM sys.database_principals WHERE name = USER_NAME();

claims.statement: DATABASE_PRINCIPAL_ID is not supported in Fabric. Look up principal_id in sys.database_principals by name instead.
claims.sql_server: DATABASE_PRINCIPAL_ID() returns the int id of the current database principal.
claims.alternative: SELECT principal_id FROM sys.database_principals WHERE name = USER_NAME();

claims.statement: SUSER_ID is not supported. SUSER_SNAME, SUSER_NAME and SUSER_SID do exist. Identify the caller by name or SID, not by a server login id.
claims.sql_server: SUSER_ID() returns the int login identification number.
claims.alternative: SELECT SUSER_SNAME() AS login_name, SUSER_SID() AS login_sid;

claims.statement: ORIGINAL_LOGIN is not supported, so audit columns that default to it will not compile. Use SUSER_SNAME() or SYSTEM_USER instead. For an Entra identity, these return the Entra name (typically a UPN such as user@tenant domain), not DOMAIN\user.
claims.sql_server: ORIGINAL_LOGIN() returns the login that opened the connection, even after impersonation.

claims.statement: SUSER_SNAME() compiles and returns nvarchar(128). For an Entra user the value is the Entra principal name (UPN), and for a service principal it is the app name or id. Do not parse it for a backslash domain prefix.
claims.sql_server: With Windows authentication the value has the form DOMAIN\user.

claims.statement: CURRENT_USER, SESSION_USER and USER_NAME() compile and return a sysname (nvarchar(128)) database user name. In Fabric this is the Entra identity name, not dbo, even for workspace admins.
claims.probe_sql: SELECT CURRENT_USER AS cu, SESSION_USER AS su, USER_NAME() AS un;
claims.sql_server: Members of sysadmin or the database owner see dbo.

claims.statement: COL_LENGTH is not supported. Read max_length from sys.columns, or use COLUMNPROPERTY with 'Precision'.
claims.sql_server: COL_LENGTH returns the defined length of a column in bytes as smallint.
claims.alternative: SELECT c.max_length FROM sys.columns AS c WHERE c.object_id = OBJECT_ID('sys.objects') AND c.name = 'name';

claims.statement: APP_NAME and HOST_NAME are not supported. Read program_name and host_name from sys.dm_exec_sessions for the current @@SPID.
claims.probe_sql: SELECT APP_NAME() AS app, HOST_NAME() AS host;
claims.sql_server: Both are commonly used in audit defaults and logging.
claims.alternative: SELECT s.program_name, s.host_name FROM sys.dm_exec_sessions AS s WHERE s.session_id = @@SPID;

claims.statement: SESSIONPROPERTY is not supported. To inspect SET options, decode @@OPTIONS, which exists.
claims.sql_server: SESSIONPROPERTY returns the setting of a SET option for the session.
claims.alternative: SELECT CASE WHEN @@OPTIONS & 32 = 32 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS ansi_nulls;

claims.statement: SERVERPROPERTY returns sql_variant. CAST the result before you concatenate or compare it, and do not assume on-premises values such as a Windows machine name or edition.
claims.sql_server: The type is also sql_variant in SQL Server, but the values describe a box product.
claims.alternative: SELECT CAST(SERVERPROPERTY('Edition') AS nvarchar(128)) AS edition;

claims.statement: DATABASEPROPERTYEX returns sql_variant. The warehouse collation it reports is typically a case-sensitive BIN2 UTF-8 collation. Name comparisons against metadata can therefore be case-sensitive, and a lookup in the wrong case silently returns nothing.
claims.sql_server: The default server collation is usually case-insensitive (for example SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS).

claims.statement: OBJECT_ID, OBJECT_NAME and SCHEMA_NAME compile and work against catalog views. OBJECT_ID returns int.
claims.probe_sql: SELECT OBJECT_ID('sys.objects') AS oid, OBJECT_NAME(OBJECT_ID('sys.objects')) AS oname, SCHEMA_NAME(1) AS sname;

claims.statement: IS_ROLEMEMBER compiles and returns int. Fabric workspace roles (Admin, Member, Contributor, Viewer) are not database roles. A workspace admin can therefore get 0 from IS_ROLEMEMBER('db_owner'), which makes role-based guards wrong without raising any error. Prefer HAS_PERMS_BY_NAME for permission checks.
claims.sql_server: The database owner and sysadmin members return 1 for db_owner.

claims.statement: @@VERSION compiles and returns nvarchar(300), but the text describes the Fabric engine, not a numbered SQL Server release. Do not parse it to branch on a SQL Server version.
claims.sql_server: Returns a string such as 'Microsoft SQL Server 2022 (RTM) ...', which scripts often parse.
